_readme: Upstream archives the engine channel is published from, each pinned by
its SHA-256. packaging/build-engine-manifest.py downloads every source
of the packages it publishes, refuses one whose digest differs from the
pin, repackages each package as one zip and lists those zips in the
signed engine manifest. scripts/check_download_sums.py holds every source
to an https address and a 64-hex digest.
The engine channel does not follow the llama.cpp tag the installers
embed (packaging/fetch-llama-server.sh): a tag is published here when
its packages are pinned below, and the publication names it.
Provenance: each digest was computed locally with `shasum -a 256` on the
downloaded archive, then compared with the digest the publisher states
(the GitHub release asset digest for llama.cpp, SHASUMS256.txt for
Node.js). The local digest is what is pinned.
`released` is the day upstream published the build. `beside` on a
source places its files flat next to the named file of an earlier
source: the CUDA runtime libraries go next to the server that loads
them. A llama-server package for Linux carries no CUDA runtime: the
one of the host is used.
To pin a tag: for each archive run
`curl -fsSL <url> -o <file> && shasum -a 256 <file>`, compare with the
publisher's digest, and add the package below.
